data.title: NZDUSD sellers stay in control as price nears the 0.54808 floor
data.description:
The NZDUSD decline started on November 10 after the pair tested the upper channel trend line and turned lower, breaking below both its 200-hour and 100-hour moving averages. The go-ahead for more downside came the next day when the price bounced back to the 200-hour moving average and sellers leaned against it. That rejection set up six days of selling that took the pair to a low of 0.54808 yesterday.

Since then, the price has been consolidating. Yesterday’s bounce stalled at 0.55057, and today’s high reached nearly the same level at 0.5506. Today’s low came in at 0.5484, just above yesterday’s low. With the pair trading near 0.5488, the price is still closer to the floor of the range than the ceiling.

data.title: The market's verdict on Nvidia earnings is a problem for the AI boom trade
data.description:
With each passing day, the probability is rising that the AI boom is coming to an end.

Nvidia reported good earnings yesterday and the guidance was upbeat. At the very least, there was no sign of trouble in the earnings numbers. Shares initially cheered, rising more than 5% after hours but that disappeared at the open and NVDA is now down 2.3% on the day.

data.title: Project to support underprivileged students completed, Elev8 broker reports
data.description:
Throughout October 2026, Elev8, a global broker, ran a charity initiative called Charity October, setting aside a fixed amount for every lot its clients traded. Elev8 covered the entire donation budget, clients didn't contribute anything, and participation was free for all.

At the end of the month, the funds were transferred to Elev8's partner, JAAGO Foundation, a Bangladesh-based non-profit that supports local communities and promotes education among underserved populations.

data.title: BoC’s Gravelle says policy scenarios help build credibility
data.description:
Bank of Canada Deputy Governor Toni Gravelle discussed how the central bank uses scenarios to explain how it might respond as economic conditions change.

  • Bank of Canada scenarios are designed to help keep the BoC accountable and build credibility.
  • When the public trusts the BoC to keep inflation around 2%, their inflation expectations stay anchored.
  • If inflation expectations are anchored, that makes monetary policy more effective.
  • By helping market participants understand how we tend to react when conditions change, we can shape their expectations.
  • Bank of Canada says scenarios help make monetary policy more effective.
  • If businesses expect the BoC will get inflation back down to 2%, they are less likely to build higher inflation into their prices.
  • That decision helps keep inflation in check and reduces barriers to getting it back to target.

data.title: USDCAD trades to the highest level for the year and going back to April 2025
data.description:
The USDCAD is pushing to new highs for the day and in the process is trading to a new high going back to April 2025. 

Fundamentally, the recent U.S.–Canada data gap favors a higher USDCAD. U.S. growth and hiring are stronger, while Canada’s latest inflation report showed less pressure underneath the headline. That gives the Fed more reason to tighten than the Bank of Canada.

data.title: As Bitcoin consolidates, the technical resistance gets closer and closer to the price. What next?
data.description:
Bitcoin continues to consolidate in a modest range, allowing the falling 100 hour moving average to catch up to the price. When Bitcoin reached its Sunday low at $61,947, the 100 hour moving average was up at $70,244 (close to $8300 above the price). Today, the moving average is down to $64,717, while Bitcoin is trading at $63,886. At today’s session high, the price nearly reached (i.e. was identical) the moving average before rotating back to the downside. That is as a result of the consolidation or breather, that the market is doing at the lower levels.  

In the video above, I take a look at the technicals, explain why traders are leaning against the 100 hour moving average, and outline the targets on a break in either direction.

data.title: Why earnings reports rarely change the bigger picture: the macro environment matters more
data.description:
Every earnings season brings a fresh wave of volatility. Companies report their quarterly results, investors reassess valuations, analysts adjust their forecasts and individual stocks can move dramatically in either direction.

Earnings reports can certainly move individual stocks, but they rarely change the broader economic and financial conditions that ultimately determine the direction of the stock market. Earnings tell you what happened in the past, while markets are constantly trying to price what might happen in the future.

data.title: Morning Kickstart: Waller makes the case for 50 bps as Nvidia lifts Nasdaq futures
data.description:
Fed Governor Chris Waller came out hawkish on CNBC this morning. He wants to break the psychology that 3% inflation is normal. He has pointed out that more than 70% of core PCE services components were running above 3% year over year in September, and he worries that demand is still firm enough for businesses to pass along price increases. His message for December was direct. If the Fed is unwilling to signal a faster pace of hikes in its statement or press conference, he favors a 50-basis-point move at the meeting. He also warned that the Fed may have to go beyond reversing last year’s cuts. marketwatch.com

The two-year Treasury yield is leading the move higher in my morning snapshot, which is where I would look first for a reaction to the Fed minutes this afternoon. In stocks, the Nasdaq 100 is getting a lift from Nvidia’s beat and raise, while Dow futures are lower. Anthropic’s expected IPO pricing is the next test of how much investors are willing to pay for AI exposure. reuters.com
